   648	def _candidate_eligibility(
   649	    pack: PackDefinition,
   650	    required_permissions: Iterable[str],
   651	    trust: _PackTrust,
   652	) -> ExecutionEligibility:
   653	    required = tuple(required_permissions)
   654	    declared = tuple(permission.id for permission in pack.permissions)
   655	    common = {
   656	        "trust_method": trust.trust_method,
   657	        "required_permissions": required,
   658	        "declared_permissions": declared,
   659	        "accepted_permissions": trust.accepted_permissions,
   660	        "active_revision": trust.active_revision,
   661	    }
   662	    if not trust.eligible:
   663	        return ExecutionEligibility(False, trust.reason, **common)
   664	
   665	    missing_declarations = sorted(set(required) - set(declared))
   666	    if missing_declarations:
   667	        return ExecutionEligibility(
   668	            False,
   669	            "manifest requires permissions not declared by its pack: "
   670	            + ", ".join(missing_declarations),
   671	            **common,
   672	        )
   673	
   674	    if trust.active_revision is not None:
   675	        missing_acceptance = sorted(set(required) - set(trust.accepted_permissions))
   676	        if missing_acceptance:
   677	            return ExecutionEligibility(
   678	                False,
   679	                "installed pack permissions were not accepted: "
   680	                + ", ".join(missing_acceptance),
   681	                **common,
   682	            )
   683	
   684	    return ExecutionEligibility(True, trust.reason, **common)

   687	def _derive_pack_trust(discovered: DiscoveredPack) -> _PackTrust:
   688	    source_kind = discovered.source_kind
   689	    if source_kind == "source":
   690	        return _PackTrust(
   691	            True,
   692	            "source-tree pack is execution-eligible",
   693	            trust_method="source_tree",
   694	        )
   695	    if source_kind == "local":
   696	        return _PackTrust(
   697	            True,
   698	            "project-local pack is execution-eligible",
   699	            trust_method="project_local",
   700	        )
   701	    if source_kind == "extra":
   702	        return _PackTrust(
   703	            True,
   704	            "pack root was explicitly supplied by the operator",
   705	            trust_method="explicit_extra_pack_root",
   706	        )
   707	    if source_kind == "env":
   708	        return _PackTrust(
   709	            False,
   710	            "environment-discovered packs are inspectable but not executable",
   711	        )
   712	    if source_kind == "installed":
   713	        return _installed_pack_trust(discovered.pack)
   714	    return _PackTrust(False, f"unknown pack source kind {source_kind!r}")

   717	def _installed_pack_trust(pack: PackDefinition) -> _PackTrust:
   718	    root = pack.root.resolve()
   719	    revision_name = root.name
   720	    if root.parent.name != "revisions":
   721	        return _PackTrust(False, "installed pack revision is outside the revisions directory")
   722	    install_root = root.parent.parent.resolve()
   723	    if install_root.name != pack.id:
   724	        return _PackTrust(False, "installed pack root does not match its pack id")
   725	
   726	    active_link = install_root / "active"
   727	    if not active_link.is_symlink():
   728	        return _PackTrust(False, "installed pack has no active revision symlink")
   729	    try:
   730	        active_revision = active_link.resolve(strict=True)
   731	    except OSError:
   732	        return _PackTrust(False, "installed pack active revision symlink is broken")
   733	    if active_revision != root:
   734	        return _PackTrust(False, "discovered installed revision is not the active revision")
   735	
   736	    record_path = root / ".astrid" / "install.json"
   737	    if not record_path.is_file():
   738	        return _PackTrust(False, "active installed revision is missing its install record")
   739	    try:
   740	        raw_record = json.loads(record_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   741	        if not isinstance(raw_record, dict):
   742	            raise TypeError("install record must be a JSON object")
   743	        record = InstallRecord.from_dict(raw_record)
   744	    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
   745	        return _PackTrust(False, f"active installed revision has a corrupt install record: {exc}")
   746	
   747	    try:
   748	        mismatch = _install_record_mismatch(
   749	            pack,
   750	            record,
   751	            install_root=install_root,
   752	            revision_name=revision_name,
   753	        )
   754	    except Exception as exc:
   755	        return _PackTrust(
   756	            False,
   757	            "active installed revision has a malformed install audit: "
   758	            f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
   759	        )
   760	    if mismatch is not None:
   761	        return _PackTrust(False, mismatch)
   762	
   763	    try:
   764	        accepted, acceptance_error = _accepted_permission_ids(pack, record)
   765	    except Exception as exc:
   766	        return _PackTrust(
   767	            False,
   768	            "active installed revision has malformed accepted permissions: "
   769	            f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
   770	        )
   771	    if acceptance_error is not None:
   772	        return _PackTrust(False, acceptance_error)
   773	
   774	    return _PackTrust(
   775	        True,
   776	        "active installed revision has a valid trust audit and accepted permissions",
   777	        trust_method=record.trust_method,
   778	        accepted_permissions=accepted,
   779	        active_revision=revision_name,
   780	    )

   783	def _install_record_mismatch(
   784	    pack: PackDefinition,
   785	    record: InstallRecord,
   786	    *,
   787	    install_root: Path,
   788	    revision_name: str,
   789	) -> str | None:
   790	    if record.pack_id != pack.id:
   791	        return "install record pack id does not match the discovered pack"
   792	    if record.version != pack.version:
   793	        return "install record version does not match the discovered pack"
   794	    if pack.schema_version and str(record.schema_version) != pack.schema_version:
   795	        return "install record schema version does not match the discovered pack"
   796	    if record.active is not True:
   797	        return "install record does not mark the active revision active"
   798	    if record.revision != revision_name:
   799	        return "install record revision does not match the active revision"
   800	    try:
   801	        recorded_install_root = Path(record.install_root).expanduser().resolve()
   802	    except (OSError, RuntimeError, TypeError, ValueError):
   803	        return "install record contains an invalid install root"
   804	    if recorded_install_root != install_root:
   805	        return "install record root does not match the active installation"
   806	    if not record.manifest_digest:
   807	        return "install record is missing its pack manifest digest"
   808	    try:
   809	        current_digest = sha256_file(pack.manifest_path)
   810	    except OSError:
   811	        return "installed pack manifest cannot be hashed"
   812	    if record.manifest_digest != current_digest:
   813	        return "install record manifest digest does not match the installed pack"
   814	    if not _valid_audit_timestamp(record.trust_acknowledged_at):
   815	        return "install record is missing a valid trust acknowledgement timestamp"
   816	    if not _valid_audit_timestamp(record.last_validation_time):
   817	        return "install record is missing a valid validation timestamp"
   818	    if not isinstance(record.trust_method, str) or not record.trust_method.strip():
   819	        return "install record is missing its trust acknowledgement method"
   820	    if record.trust_method not in _INSTALL_TRUST_METHODS:
   821	        return "install record contains an unknown trust acknowledgement method"
   822	    if not isinstance(record.trust_actor, str) or not record.trust_actor.strip():
   823	        return "install record is missing its trust acknowledgement actor"
   824	    if record.no_sandbox_warning_version != _INSTALL_WARNING_VERSION:
   825	        return "install record does not contain the current no-sandbox acknowledgement"
   826	    if not isinstance(record.trust_summary, dict) or not record.trust_summary:
   827	        return "install record is missing its trust summary"
   828	    if record.trust_summary.get("pack_id") != pack.id:
   829	        return "install trust summary does not match the discovered pack"
   830	    trust_block = record.trust_summary.get("trust")
   831	    if not isinstance(trust_block, dict):
   832	        return "install trust summary is missing its trust disclosure"
   833	    if (
   834	        trust_block.get("sandbox") != "none"
   835	        or trust_block.get("runs_with_user_process_permissions") is not True
   836	        or trust_block.get("permission_enforcement") != "disclosure_only"
   837	    ):
   838	        return "install trust summary contains an invalid trust disclosure"
   839	    return None

   842	def _valid_audit_timestamp(value: object) -> bool:
   843	    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
   844	        return False
   845	    try:
   846	        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
   847	    except ValueError:
   848	        return False
   849	    return parsed.tzinfo is not None

   852	def _accepted_permission_ids(
   853	    pack: PackDefinition,
   854	    record: InstallRecord,
   855	) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], str | None]:
   856	    accepted_raw = record.permissions_accepted
   857	    if not isinstance(accepted_raw, list):
   858	        return (), "install record permissions_accepted must be an array"
   859	    if any(not isinstance(item, dict) for item in accepted_raw):
   860	        return (), "install record contains a malformed accepted permission"
   861	
   862	    expected = [permission.to_dict() for permission in pack.permissions]
   863	    if accepted_raw != expected:
   864	        return (), "install record accepted permissions do not match the installed pack"
   865	    if record.trust_summary.get("permissions") != accepted_raw:
   866	        return (), "install trust summary permissions do not match the accepted permissions"
   867	
   868	    accepted_ids = tuple(str(item["id"]) for item in accepted_raw)
   869	    if len(accepted_ids) != len(set(accepted_ids)):
   870	        return (), "install record contains duplicate accepted permissions"
   871	    return accepted_ids, None

   874	def _build_alias_resolvers(
   875	    discovered: tuple[DiscoveredPack, ...],
   876	    *,
   877	    kind: str,
   878	    pack_trust: Mapping[int, _PackTrust],
   879	    registry: _RenderingRegistry[Any],
   880	    error_type: type[RenderingRegistryError],
   881	    programmatic_aliases: Iterable[tuple[str, str]] = (),
   882	) -> tuple[AliasResolver, AliasResolver]:
   883	    # Validate every discovered alias graph, including inspect-only packs.  A
   884	    # separate trusted resolver is then built so environment/corrupt install
   885	    # metadata cannot redirect executable capability resolution.

   923	def _populate_alias_resolver(

   925	    discovered: tuple[DiscoveredPack, ...],

   929	    pack_trust: Mapping[int, _PackTrust],
   930	    registry: _RenderingRegistry[Any],
   931	) -> None:
   932	    # Alias collisions follow the same precedence as candidates.  Register
   933	    # lowest-precedence packs first so a lower priority_index wins last.
   934	    for item in reversed(discovered):

   950	def _alias_target_can_participate(
   951	    alias: Mapping[str, Any],
   952	    registry: _RenderingRegistry[Any],
   953	) -> bool:
   954	    """Keep aliases to unknown/chained ids, but skip known denied targets.
   955	
   956	    An alias-only compatibility pack may legitimately point at a backend from
   957	    another pack, so absence is not grounds for dropping the declaration.
   958	    When the direct target was discovered and every candidate was denied,
   959	    however, letting that alias win would reintroduce the shadowing problem
   960	    that the executable-only registry is designed to prevent.
   961	    """
   962	
   963	    target = alias.get("canonical_id")
   964	    if not isinstance(target, str):
   965	        return True
   966	    discovered = registry._discovered.get(target)
   967	    return discovered is None or target in registry._entries

     1	# CapabilityRegistry — kernel base contract
     2	
     3	## 1. Overview
     4	
     5	`CapabilityRegistry[K, T]` is the generic base class shared by the three layered
     6	registries:
     7	
     8	- `ExecutorRegistry`  (`astrid/core/executor/registry.py`)
     9	- `OrchestratorRegistry` (`astrid/core/orchestrator/registry.py`)
    10	- `ElementRegistry`  (`astrid/core/element/registry.py`)
    11	
    12	Each subclass specialises in a single capability kind (executor, orchestrator,
    13	element), but the storage shape, sort-then-pick-first winner strategy, and
    14	public read surface are identical.  The kernel base captures that shared
    15	contract without forcing every subclass into a single `register()` or `get()`
    16	signature.
    17	
    18	## 2. Storage: `_entries: dict[K, list[T]]`
    19	
    20	Every registry stores a flat dictionary where each key maps to an **ordered
    21	list** of definitions.  The order is the priority rank — index `[0]` is always
    22	the winning definition; indices `[1:]` are shadowed.
    23	
    24	| Registry | Key type `K` | Example key |
    25	|---|---|---|
    26	| Executor | `str` (executor id) | `"transcribe"` |
    27	| Orchestrator | `str` (orchestrator id) | `"scenes"` |
    28	| Element | `tuple[str, str]` (`(kind, element_id)`) | `("text_card", "default")` |
    29	
    30	Sort discipline:
    31	
    32	- **Executor / Orchestrator:** `int(d.metadata.get("priority", 30))` ascending.
    33	  Lower numeric priority = higher precedence.
    34	- **Element:** `(priority, source, str(root))` tuple ascending.
    35	  Priority is a dataclass field, not metadata.
    36	
    37	The base declares `_entries: dict[K, list[T]]` in `__init__` and relies on
    38	subclass `register()` to maintain sort order.  No public mutator exists on the
    39	base — callers iterate through `register()` on each subclass.
    40	
    41	## 3. Public surface (provided by the base)
    42	
    43	| Method | Returns | Description |
    44	|---|---|---|
    45	| `list(kind: Optional[str] = None)` | `tuple[T, ...]` | Winners only (index `[0]` of each entry), optionally filtered by `kind`, sorted by id.  Executor/Orchestrator validate `kind` ∈ `{"built_in", "external"}`; Element passes `kind` through `element_kind_registry.normalize()`. |
    46	| `as_mapping()` | `MappingProxyType[K, T]` | Immutable key → winner mapping for fast lookups across the whole registry. |
    47	| `conflicts()` | `tuple[Conflict, ...]` | Entries where `len(definitions) > 1`.  Returns winner + shadowed tuple.  Element returns `ElementConflict` (kind + id); Executor/Orchestrator will receive an analogous shape. |
    48	
    49	### Intentional omissions
    50	
    51	- **No public `register()` on the base.**  SD2: Each subclass accepts different
    52	  input types:
    53	  - Executor/Orchestrator: `Definition | dict[str, Any]` — validates inside
    54	    `register()` via `validate_*_definition()`.
    55	  - Element: `ElementDefinition` only (already validated at load time).
    56	  A uniform base signature would force validation into a hook that doesn't fit
    57	  element's pre-validated pipeline.
    58	
    59	- **No public `get()` on the base.**  SD3: Override assembly lives in subclass
    60	  `get()`.  The base provides a protected `_resolve_override_key()` helper,
    61	  but each subclass decides how to annotate/return the resolved definition:
    62	  - Executor/Orchestrator return the override target definition directly.
    63	  - Element wraps the target with `dataclasses.replace(..., metadata={...,
    64	    "override_target": target_id})` so callers can trace the remapping.
    65	
    66	## 4. Protected helpers (provided by the base)
    67	
    68	| Helper | Signature | Purpose |
    69	|---|---|---|
    70	| `_resolve_entry` | `(entry: list[T] \| T) -> T` | Return the winner.  Handles legacy scalar values (someone assigned directly to `_executors[id] = def`) by returning the scalar as-is. |
    71	| `_iter_entries` | `(entry: list[T] \| T) -> Iterable[T]` | Yield every definition — winner + shadowed.  Used by `_iter_all()` and validation loops that need to inspect the full set. |
    72	| `_winner_for` | `(key: K) -> T` | Shorthand for `_resolve_entry(self._entries[key])`.  DRY's up the `entries[key][0]` pattern. |
    73	| `_resolve_override_key` | `(capability_kind: str, key: K) -> K \| None` | Consults `self.override_store` (if set) and returns the remapped key, or `None` if no override exists.  The returned key may be the same as the input (no-op override).  Used by subclass `get()`. |
    74	
    75	### Helper that stays subclass-only
    76	
    77	`_resolve_requested_id(capability_id: str) -> str` resolves an alias to a
    78	canonical registry key via `self.alias_resolver`.  It raises `KeyError` when
    79	the id (or its resolved target) is absent.  This logic is shared by Executor
    80	and Orchestrator but does **not** fit Element (which keys on `(kind, id)`
    81	tuples and delegates kind normalisation to `element_kind_registry`).  The base
    82	must not assume alias resolution; subclasses that need it keep their own copy.
    83	
    84	## 5. What each subclass brings
    85	
    86	| Concern | Who owns it |
    87	|---|---|
    88	| Input validation (`validate_*_definition`) | Subclass `register()` |
    89	| Type-specific key shape (`str` vs `tuple[str, str]`) | Subclass `__init__` |
    90	| Alias resolution (`_resolve_requested_id`) | Executor/Orchestrator (not Element) |
    91	| Override assembly / metadata annotation | Subclass `get()` |
    92	| `fork()` | Subclass (deep fork, local pack plumbing) |
    93	| `validate_all()` (graph refs, cycles, etc.) | Subclass (executor/orchestrator cross-references) |
    94	| `to_dict()` / `to_json()` | Subclass (different top-level key names) |
    95	| `_validate_child_*` / `_strict_child_type_check` | Orchestrator only |
    96	
    97	## 6. Design rationale (decisions locked by SD1–SD3)
    98	
    99	- **SD1** (`ModelRegistry` exempt): `ModelRegistry` uses a flat `dict[str,
   100	  ModelEntry]` with no multi-source layering, no priority sort, no
   101	  alias/override hooks.  It loads from a static YAML via `@classmethod` and
   102	  never calls `register()`.  Forcing it onto the `dict[K, list[T]]` shape
   103	  would add indirection for zero benefit.
   104	
   105	- **SD2** (no public `register()` on base): Each subclass owns its validation.
   106	  Executor/Orchestrator accept `Definition | dict`; Element accepts only
   107	  `ElementDefinition`.  A shared `register()` would need a callback hook and
   108	  would still differ in key construction.
   109	
   110	- **SD3** (no public `get()` on base): Override resolution is per-subclass.
   111	  Element annotates the returned definition with `override_target` metadata via
   112	  `dataclasses.replace`; executor/orchestrator return targets directly.
   113	  Lifting override assembly into the base would lose element's annotation
   114	  behaviour.
   115	
   116	## 7. Non-goals
   117	
   118	- The base does **not** own `fork()` — it requires executor/orchestrator
   119	  metadata fields (`content_root`, `executor_root`, `orchestrator_root`)
   120	  that differ across subclasses.
   121	- The base does **not** own alias discovery or pack loading —
   122	  `load_default_registry()` is per-subclass module-level code.
   123	- The base does **not** enforce a particular sort key — subclasses provide
   124	  their own `key=` lambda inside `register()`.

@@ -410,6 +410,37 @@ class PackDiscoveryMetadataTest(unittest.TestCase):
 
         self.assertEqual([p.id for p in ordered], ["alpha"])
 
+    def test_rendering_consumers_receive_source_kind_and_priority_metadata(self) -> None:
+        """Rendering registries consume metadata, not the compatibility wrapper
+        that drops source/priority context."""
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            root = Path(tmp)
+            source_pack = _make_pack(root / "source", "source_pack")
+            extra_root = root / "extra"
+            extra_pack = _make_pack(extra_root, "extra_pack")
+
+            def scan(arg=None):
+                if arg is None:
+                    return (source_pack,)
+                if Path(arg).resolve() == extra_root.resolve():
+                    return (extra_pack,)
+                return ()
+
+            discovered = discover_pack_metadata(
+                project_root=root / "project",
+                extra_pack_roots=(str(extra_root),),
+                include_installed=False,
+                discover_packs_fn=scan,
+            )
+
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [(item.id, item.source_kind, item.priority_index) for item in discovered],
+            [
+                ("source_pack", "source", 0),
+                ("extra_pack", "extra", 1),
+            ],
+        )
+
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":

+class TestDefaultRegistryOverrideStoreWiring:
+    """Default factories load project-persisted overrides themselves."""
+
+    def test_executor_default_factory_uses_project_override_store(self):
+        from astrid.core.execution.executor import registry as executor_registry_module
+        from astrid.core.execution.executor.schema import ExecutorDefinition
+
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            store = OverrideStore(tmp)
+            store.set_override("executor", "fixture.original", "fixture.replacement")
+            definitions = (
+                ExecutorDefinition(
+                    id="fixture.original",
+                    name="Original",
+                    kind="built_in",
+                    version="1.0.0",
+                ),
+                ExecutorDefinition(
+                    id="fixture.replacement",
+                    name="Replacement",
+                    kind="built_in",
+                    version="1.0.0",
+                ),
+            )
+
+            with (
+                mock.patch.object(
+                    executor_registry_module,
+                    "_discover_executor_packs",
+                    return_value=(),
+                ),
+                mock.patch.object(
+                    executor_registry_module,
+                    "_load_pack_executors_from_packs",
+                    return_value=definitions,
+                ),
+            ):
+                registry = executor_registry_module.load_default_registry(
+                    project_root=tmp,
+                    include_installed=False,
+                )
+
+            assert registry.override_store is not None
+            assert registry.get("fixture.original").id == "fixture.replacement"
+
+    def test_orchestrator_default_factory_uses_project_override_store(self):
+        from astrid.core.execution.executor.registry import ExecutorRegistry
+        from astrid.core.execution.orchestrator import registry as orchestrator_registry_module
+        from astrid.core.execution.orchestrator.schema import (
+            OrchestratorDefinition,
+            RuntimeSpec,
+        )
+
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            store = OverrideStore(tmp)
+            store.set_override(
+                "orchestrator",
+                "fixture.original",
+                "fixture.replacement",
+            )
+            definitions = (
+                OrchestratorDefinition(
+                    id="fixture.original",
+                    name="Original",
+                    kind="built_in",
+                    version="1.0.0",
+                    runtime=RuntimeSpec(kind="python", function="run"),
+                ),
+                OrchestratorDefinition(
+                    id="fixture.replacement",
+                    name="Replacement",
+                    kind="built_in",
+                    version="1.0.0",
+                    runtime=RuntimeSpec(kind="python", function="run"),
+                ),
+            )
+
+            with (
+                mock.patch.object(
+                    orchestrator_registry_module,
+                    "_discover_orchestrator_packs",
+                    return_value=(),
+                ),
+                mock.patch.object(
+                    orchestrator_registry_module,
+                    "_load_pack_orchestrators_from_packs",
+                    return_value=definitions,
+                ),
+            ):
+                registry = orchestrator_registry_module.load_default_registry(
+                    executor_registry=ExecutorRegistry(),
+                    project_root=tmp,
+                    include_installed=False,
+                )
+
+            assert registry.override_store is not None
+            assert registry.get("fixture.original").id == "fixture.replacement"

.oracle/findings/01-pack-discovery-trust.txt:3:**1. Precedence order** — `SOURCE_KINDS = ("source","local","extra","env","installed")` (discovery.py:31). `discover_pack_metadata()` (discovery.py:79-164) walks exactly that order: repo source packs (115-118), project `local` pack (120-123), `extra_pack_roots` (133-139), `ASTRID_PACKS_PATH` roots (140-149), then `installed_pack_roots()` (150-162). `priority_index` = list position, lower wins (106-113). Per-root scanner: `discover_packs()` (loader.py:84-107), raises on duplicate ids (103-104). **Active installed revisions** = resolved `active` symlink via `active_pack_roots()` (store.py:195-216, 121-133); `InstallRecord.active` bool exists (store.py:56, 318-351) but discovery keys off the symlink only; `mark_inactive()` unlinks it (store.py:231-237).
.oracle/findings/01-pack-discovery-trust.txt:5:**2. Trust** — No `trusted` field exists (grep: 0 hits). Trust is procedural: `validate_pack` gate (install_local.py:199-215), exact-phrase acknowledgement `_confirm_trust` (install_trust.py:202-214), audit labels `trust_method/actor/acknowledged_at/tier`, `permissions_accepted` (store.py:72-79; install_local.py:404-433). `trust_tier` = source type only (install_local.py:292-293). Downloaded-but-uninstalled packs sit in `staging/` (store.py:135-137) with no `active` symlink → **not discoverable, not executable**; staging is cleaned on failure (install_local.py:263-268, 348).
.oracle/findings/01-pack-discovery-trust.txt:9:**4. Result shape** — `tuple[DiscoveredPack]` (discovery.py:35-76): `pack`, `source_kind`, `priority_index`, props `id`/`pack_dir`/`executor_roots()`/`orchestrator_roots()`/`element_roots()`/`skill_roots()`. No `active` field. Callers: element/registry.py:207,303; skills/discovery.py:143 (filters extra/installed); sdk/discovery.py:140; generation verbs/features/backends; render/run.py:1161; executor+orchestrator use `discover_packs_ordered` (executor/registry.py:294) which drops source_kind.
.oracle/findings/01-pack-discovery-trust.txt:12:- Order: source < local < extra < env < installed (discovery.py:31,115-162)
.oracle/findings/01-pack-discovery-trust.txt:24:- Executor/orchestrator registries auto-execute every discovered pack (incl. env/extra/installed) with no trust filter; permissions never enforced — installed code runs with user process permissions.
.oracle/findings/01-pack-discovery-trust.txt:28:Add a trust gate at the discovery→registry boundary: only packs with a verified install record (acknowledged trust + digest) are executable; treat source/local/extra/env as untrusted for the plugin surface. Since permissions are unenforced, default-deny (refuse execution) until a runtime permission enforcement layer exists.
.oracle/findings/09-parity-fixtures-tests-ci.txt:9:**4. CI lanes** — `ci.yml`: ffmpeg installed (:32–35); real render only inside pytest; Remotion typecheck blocking (:83–89); advisory `continue-on-error` steps (:49–51, :59–61). No job sets `ASTRID_RENDERER_PARITY`. `Makefile` `check` (:19), `ci` (:43) — no parity target. Markers registered in `pyproject.toml:154–165`.

   222	
   223	Minimum capability manifest fields needed by the target contract, whether they
   224	live in executor, orchestrator, or element schemas:
   225	
   226	- canonical id, local id, and owning pack id;
   227	- capability kind;
   228	- status and visibility;
   229	- aliases and deprecation metadata, once alias support exists;
   230	- provenance/source metadata;
   231	- inspectable inputs and outputs where the kind supports them;
   232	- safety/cost/secrets/network declarations.
   233	
   234	## Current Pack Listing
   235	
   236	The canonical runtime pack listing and per-pack taxonomy assignments are
   237	maintained in **[pack-taxonomy.md](pack-taxonomy.md)**. See that document's
   238	domain table and Example Packs section for the current `astrid/packs/`
   239	inventory, shell classifications (`_core`, `builtin`), and example packs under
   240	`examples/packs/`.
   241	
   242	### Mapping Contract Axes to Taxonomy Fields
   243	
   244	The six conceptual axes defined in §Pack Axes above map onto
   245	`pack-taxonomy.md`'s six machine-readable fields as follows:
   246	
   247	| Contract Axis | Taxonomy Field |
   248	|---|---|
   249	| Namespace / id prefix | `id` (pack-level), `domain` (grouping axis) |
   250	| Distribution / source | `origin` |
   251	| Enablement | `install_tier` |
   252	| Ownership / support | `support` |
   253	| Maturity / status | `stability` |
   254	| Trust / safety profile | `permissions` block (pack-level, not a taxonomy enum) |
   255	
   256	The trust/safety axis is expressed through the `permissions` block in
   257	`pack.yaml` rather than a single taxonomy enum, since safety posture is
   258	multi-dimensional (network access, secrets, paid APIs, external binaries).
   259	
   260	Element precedence remains the current implementation precedent:
   261	
   262	1. Active theme elements override other sources when an active theme is set.
   263	2. Project `local` pack forks override bundled pack elements when a distinct
   264	   project root is used.
   265	3. Bundled pack elements provide the fallback managed implementation.
   266	
   267	That precedence is documentation of current behavior, not a command to move
   268	elements during M0. Later fork/override work should reuse this ordering where it
   269	fits executors, orchestrators, and whole packs.
   270	
   271	## Deferred Scope
   272	
   273	M0 deliberately does not implement:
   274	
   275	- pack enable/disable mechanics;
   276	- discovery filtering or `--all` behavior;
   277	- alias resolution;
   278	- alias manifests or alias validation;
   279	- public id moves;
   280	- remote or hosted registries;
   281	- package installation from remote sources;
   282	- pack directory moves;
   283	- fork/update commands;
   284	- fork/update reports;
   285	- dependency isolation;
   286	- semantic merge/update intelligence;
   287	- rich capability graph planning;
   288	- runtime enforcement of every safety declaration;
   289	- broad cleanup of generated or example packs.

   200	def test_static_load_and_read_surface_never_imports_fixture_backend_modules(
   201	    tmp_path: Path,
   202	) -> None:
   203	    """The full static surface leaves no fixture backend module in sys.modules.
   204	
   205	    Discovery, listing, inspection, conflict reporting, and evidence
   206	    resolution may only read YAML/JSON data.  After exercising every read
   207	    API, no module backed by a fixture pack directory may appear.
   208	    """
   209	    modules_before = set(sys.modules)
   210	
   211	    with _load_with_source(tmp_path / "project") as (renderers, planners, finalizers):
   212	        renderers.get("rendering.remotion")
   213	        renderers.get("ffmpeg")
   214	        renderers.list()
   215	        renderers.inspect("rendering.remotion")
   216	        renderers.candidates()
   217	        renderers.candidates("rendering.remotion", eligible=True)
   218	        renderers.conflicts()
   219	        renderers.resolve_evidence("remotion")
   220	        renderers.validate_all()
   221	        planners.list()
   222	        finalizers.list()
   223	
   224	    modules_after = set(sys.modules)
   225	    new_modules = modules_after - modules_before
   226	
   227	    assert "backend_should_not_import" not in sys.modules
   228	    assert not any("backend_should_not_import" in name for name in new_modules)
   229	    assert not any("renderer_packs" in name for name in new_modules)
   230	    fixture_root = str(FIXTURES.resolve())
   231	    for name in new_modules:
   232	        module = sys.modules.get(name)
   233	        module_file = getattr(module, "__file__", None)
   234	        assert module_file is None or not str(Path(module_file).resolve()).startswith(
   235	            fixture_root
   236	        ), f"module {name!r} is backed by a fixture pack file: {module_file}"

   279	def test_cross_layer_precedence_winner_is_recorded_in_evidence_and_conflicts(
   280	    tmp_path: Path,
   281	) -> None:
   282	    """The higher-precedence layer wins and the evidence records it.
   283	
   284	    ``priority_index`` is the discovery-order position: lower indices are
   285	    discovered first and therefore outrank later layers.  Both the winner's
   286	    ``resolve_evidence`` payload and the conflict report must record the
   287	    same outcome.
   288	    """
   289	    source_root = tmp_path / "source"
   290	    extra_root = tmp_path / "extra"
   291	    _write_renderer_pack(source_root, "shared_render", renderer_name="Source Winner")
   292	    _write_renderer_pack(extra_root, "shared_render", renderer_name="Extra Shadow")
   293	
   294	    with _load_with_source(
   295	        tmp_path / "project",
   296	        source_root,
   297	        extra_pack_roots=(str(extra_root),),
   298	    ) as (renderers, _, _):
   299	        winner = renderers.get("shared_render.renderer")
   300	        evidence = renderers.resolve_evidence("shared_render.renderer")
   301	        conflicts = renderers.conflicts()
   302	
   303	    assert winner.manifest.name == "Source Winner"
   304	    assert winner.priority_index == 0
   305	    assert winner.source_kind == "source"
   306	
   307	    assert evidence["resolved_id"] == "shared_render.renderer"
   308	    assert evidence["source_kind"] == "source"
   309	    assert evidence["pack_id"] == "shared_render"
   310	    assert evidence["priority"] == 0
   311	    assert evidence["priority_index"] == 0
   312	    assert evidence["eligible"] is True
   313	    assert evidence["eligibility_reason"] == "source-tree pack is execution-eligible"
   314	    assert evidence["alias_chain"] == []
   315	    assert evidence["override"] is None
   316	
   317	    assert len(conflicts) == 1
   318	    assert conflicts[0].key == "shared_render.renderer"
   319	    assert conflicts[0].winner.manifest.name == "Source Winner"
   320	    assert [candidate.manifest.name for candidate in conflicts[0].shadowed] == [
   321	        "Extra Shadow"
   322	    ]

   353	def test_ineligible_duplicate_manifest_is_excluded_from_conflicts_and_execution(
   354	    tmp_path: Path,
   355	) -> None:
   356	    """An ineligible duplicate never becomes a shadowed alternate.
   357	
   358	    Only execution-eligible candidates enter the executable registry, so a
   359	    same-id duplicate that fails eligibility produces no conflict record and
   360	    cannot influence the winner.
   361	    """
   362	    source_root = tmp_path / "source"
   363	    _write_renderer_pack(
   364	        source_root,
   365	        "conflict_render",
   366	        renderer_name="Eligible First",
   367	        duplicate_name="Denied Second",
   368	    )
   369	    duplicate = source_root / "conflict_render" / "manifests" / "b.renderer.yaml"
   370	    duplicate.write_text(
   371	        duplicate.read_text(encoding="utf-8") + "required_permissions: [network]\n",
   372	        encoding="utf-8",
   373	    )
   374	
   375	    with _load_with_source(tmp_path / "project", source_root) as (renderers, _, _):
   376	        discovered = renderers.inspect("conflict_render.renderer")
   377	        conflicts = renderers.conflicts()
   378	        eligible = renderers.candidates("conflict_render.renderer", eligible=True)
   379	        winner = renderers.get("conflict_render.renderer")
   380	
   381	    assert [candidate.manifest.name for candidate in discovered] == [
   382	        "Eligible First",
   383	        "Denied Second",
   384	    ]
   385	    assert [candidate.execution_eligible for candidate in discovered] == [True, False]
   386	    assert conflicts == ()
   387	    assert [candidate.manifest.name for candidate in eligible] == ["Eligible First"]
   388	    assert winner.manifest.name == "Eligible First"

    21	def _optional_pack_aliases(value: Any, *, path: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], ...]:
    22	    if value is None:
    23	        return ()
    24	    if not isinstance(value, list):
    25	        raise PackValidationError(f"{path} must be an array")
    26	
    27	    normalized: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    28	    allowed_keys = {"alias", "canonical_id", "kind", "deprecated", "deprecation_message"}
    29	    for index, raw_alias in enumerate(value):
    30	        alias_path = f"{path}[{index}]"
    31	        if not isinstance(raw_alias, dict):
    32	            raise PackValidationError(f"{alias_path} must be an object")
    33	        unknown_keys = sorted(set(raw_alias) - allowed_keys)
    34	        if unknown_keys:
    35	            raise PackValidationError(
    36	                f"{alias_path} has unknown field(s): {', '.join(unknown_keys)}"
    37	            )
    38	
    39	        kind = _require_string(raw_alias, "kind", f"{alias_path}.kind")
    40	        if kind not in PACK_ALIAS_KINDS:
    41	            raise PackValidationError(
    42	                f"{alias_path}.kind must be one of {list(PACK_ALIAS_KINDS)}"
    43	            )
    44	
    45	        alias = _require_string(raw_alias, "alias", f"{alias_path}.alias")
    46	        qualified_id_pack_id(alias, path=f"{alias_path}.alias")
    47	        canonical_id = _require_string(raw_alias, "canonical_id", f"{alias_path}.canonical_id")
    48	        qualified_id_pack_id(canonical_id, path=f"{alias_path}.canonical_id")
    49	
    50	        normalized_alias: dict[str, Any] = {
    51	            "kind": kind,
    52	            "alias": alias,
    53	            "canonical_id": canonical_id,
    54	        }
    55	        if "deprecated" in raw_alias:
    56	            deprecated = raw_alias["deprecated"]
    57	            if not isinstance(deprecated, bool):
    58	                raise PackValidationError(f"{alias_path}.deprecated must be a boolean")
    59	            normalized_alias["deprecated"] = deprecated
    60	        if "deprecation_message" in raw_alias:
    61	            deprecation_message = raw_alias["deprecation_message"]
    62	            if not isinstance(deprecation_message, str):
    63	                raise PackValidationError(f"{alias_path}.deprecation_message must be a string")
    64	            normalized_alias["deprecation_message"] = deprecation_message
    65	        normalized.append(normalized_alias)
    66	
    67	    return tuple(normalized)

+def pack_rendering_manifest_paths(
+    pack: "PackDefinition",
+) -> tuple[tuple[Path, ...], tuple[Path, ...], tuple[Path, ...]]:
+    """Return contained renderer, planner, and finalizer manifest paths.
+
+    Rendering extensions name manifests relative to the pack root. Resolving
+    every path before returning it also rejects traversal and symlink escapes.
+    """
+    rendering = pack.extensions.get("rendering", {})
+    renderers = _resolve_pack_rendering_manifest_paths(
+        pack,
+        rendering.get("renderers", ()),
+        kind="renderers",
+    )
+    planners = _resolve_pack_rendering_manifest_paths(
+        pack,
+        rendering.get("planners", ()),
+        kind="planners",
+    )
+    finalizers = _resolve_pack_rendering_manifest_paths(
+        pack,
+        rendering.get("finalizers", ()),
+        kind="finalizers",
+    )
+    return renderers, planners, finalizers
+
+
+def _resolve_pack_rendering_manifest_paths(
+    pack: "PackDefinition",
+    paths: Iterable[str],
+    *,
+    kind: str,
+) -> tuple[Path, ...]:
+    root = pack.root.resolve()
+    resolved_paths: list[Path] = []
+    for index, raw_path in enumerate(paths):
+        relative_path = Path(raw_path)
+        resolved = (root / relative_path).resolve()
+        if relative_path.is_absolute() or not resolved.is_relative_to(root):
+            raise PackValidationError(
+                f"pack.extensions.rendering.{kind}[{index}] must stay within the pack root"
+            )
+        resolved_paths.append(resolved)
+    return tuple(resolved_paths)
+

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path

+from referencing import Registry, Resource
+
+from astrid.core.pack import PackValidationError, load_pack_manifest
+from astrid.core.pack.alias_resolver import extract_pack_aliases

+
+
+SCHEMAS_ROOT = (
+    Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "astrid" / "core" / "pack" / "schemas" / "v1"
+)
+
+
+def _write_pack(tmp_path: Path, body: str, *, pack_id: str = "render_pack") -> Path:
+    pack_root = tmp_path / pack_id
+    pack_root.mkdir()
+    manifest_path = pack_root / "pack.yaml"
+    manifest_path.write_text(body, encoding="utf-8")
+    return manifest_path
+
+
+def _schema_errors(body: str) -> list[str]:
+    pack_schema = json.loads((SCHEMAS_ROOT / "pack.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    defs_schema = json.loads((SCHEMAS_ROOT / "_defs.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    registry = Registry().with_resource("_defs.json", Resource.from_contents(defs_schema))
+    validator = jsonschema.Draft7Validator(pack_schema, registry=registry)
+    return [error.message for error in validator.iter_errors(yaml.safe_load(body))]
+
+
+def test_rendering_extensions_round_trip_through_schema_and_normalizer(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    body = """schema_version: 1
+id: render_pack
+name: Rendering Pack
+version: 1.0.0
+extensions:
+  rendering:
+    renderers:
+      - rendering/remotion.renderer.yaml
+      - rendering/ffmpeg.renderer.json
+    planners:
+      - rendering/hybrid.planner.yaml
+    finalizers:
+      - rendering/ffmpeg.finalizer.yaml
+"""
+    expected = {
+        "renderers": [
+            "rendering/remotion.renderer.yaml",
+            "rendering/ffmpeg.renderer.json",
+        ],
+        "planners": ["rendering/hybrid.planner.yaml"],
+        "finalizers": ["rendering/ffmpeg.finalizer.yaml"],
+    }
+
+    assert _schema_errors(body) == []
+    pack = load_pack_manifest(_write_pack(tmp_path, body))
+    assert pack.extensions["rendering"] == expected
+    assert pack.to_dict()["extensions"]["rendering"] == expected
+
+
+def test_rendering_extensions_reject_unknown_keys_in_schema_and_normalizer(
+    tmp_path: Path,
+) -> None:
+    body = """schema_version: 1
+id: render_pack
+name: Rendering Pack
+version: 1.0.0
+extensions:
+  rendering:
+    renderers: []
+    backends: []
+"""
+
+    assert _schema_errors(body)
+    with pytest.raises(
+        PackValidationError,
+        match=r"pack\.extensions\.rendering has unknown field\(s\): backends",
+    ):
+        load_pack_manifest(_write_pack(tmp_path, body))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("declared_path", ["../outside.renderer.yaml", "/tmp/outside.renderer.yaml"])
+def test_rendering_manifest_paths_reject_pack_root_escapes(
+    tmp_path: Path,
+    declared_path: str,
+) -> None:
+    body = f"""schema_version: 1
+id: render_pack
+name: Rendering Pack
+version: 1.0.0
+extensions:
+  rendering:
+    renderers:
+      - {declared_path}
+"""
+    pack = load_pack_manifest(_write_pack(tmp_path, body))
+
+    with pytest.raises(PackValidationError, match="must stay within the pack root"):
+        pack_rendering_manifest_paths(pack)
+
+
+def test_rendering_manifest_paths_resolve_relative_to_pack_root(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    body = """schema_version: 1
+id: render_pack
+name: Rendering Pack
+version: 1.0.0
+extensions:
+  rendering:
+    renderers:
+      - manifests/renderer.yaml
+    planners:
+      - manifests/planner.yaml
+    finalizers:
+      - manifests/finalizer.yaml
+"""
+    pack = load_pack_manifest(_write_pack(tmp_path, body))
+
+    renderers, planners, finalizers = pack_rendering_manifest_paths(pack)
+    assert renderers == (pack.root / "manifests" / "renderer.yaml",)
+    assert planners == (pack.root / "manifests" / "planner.yaml",)
+    assert finalizers == (pack.root / "manifests" / "finalizer.yaml",)
+
+
+def test_extract_pack_aliases_recognizes_rendering_alias_kinds(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    body = """schema_version: 1
+id: render_pack
+name: Rendering Pack
+version: 1.0.0
+aliases:
+  - kind: renderer
+    alias: render_pack.legacy_renderer
+    canonical_id: render_pack.renderer
+  - kind: planner
+    alias: render_pack.legacy_planner
+    canonical_id: render_pack.planner
+  - kind: finalizer
+    alias: render_pack.legacy_finalizer
+    canonical_id: render_pack.finalizer
+"""
+    assert _schema_errors(body) == []
+    pack = load_pack_manifest(_write_pack(tmp_path, body))
+
+    for kind in ("renderer", "planner", "finalizer"):
+        aliases = extract_pack_aliases((pack,), kind=kind)
+        assert aliases["render_pack"] == [
+            {
+                "kind": kind,
+                "alias": f"render_pack.legacy_{kind}",
+                "canonical_id": f"render_pack.{kind}",
+                "source_pack_id": "render_pack",
+            }
+        ]

    16	
    17	
    18	def build_plan_v2(
    19	    *,
    20	    python_exec: str,
    21	    run_root: str | Path,
    22	    target_run_id: str,
    23	    repo_root: str | Path | None = None,
    24	    run_id: str | None = None,
    25	) -> dict[str, Any]:
    26	    """Build a task plan for prepare → assemble → render iteration-video work."""
    27	
    28	    run_root = Path(run_root)
    29	    plan_id = f"iteration-video-{run_id or uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}"
    30	    cmd_prepare = _build_prepare_cmd(python_exec, run_root, target_run_id, repo_root)
    31	    cmd_assemble = _build_assemble_cmd(python_exec, run_root, repo_root)
    32	    cmd_render = _build_render_cmd(python_exec, run_root)
    33	    local_zero = cost_entry(0, source="local")
    34	
    35	    return build_plan_template(
    36	        plan_id=plan_id,
    37	        steps=[
    38	            build_leaf_template(
    39	                "prepare",
    40	                command=cmd_prepare,
    41	                produces=[
    42	                    file_output("manifest", "iteration.manifest.json"),
    43	                    file_output("quality", "iteration.quality.json"),
    44	                ],
    45	                cost=local_zero,
    46	            ),
    47	            build_leaf_template(
    48	                "assemble",
    49	                command=cmd_assemble,
    50	                produces=[
    51	                    file_output("timeline", "iteration.timeline.json"),
    52	                    file_output("manifest", "iteration.manifest.json"),
    53	                    file_output("report", "iteration.report.html"),
    54	                    file_output("quality", "iteration.quality.json"),
    55	                    file_output("hype_timeline", "hype.timeline.json"),
    56	                    file_output("hype_assets", "hype.assets.json"),
    57	                ],
    58	                cost=local_zero,
    59	            ),
    60	            build_leaf_template(
    61	                "render",
    62	                command=cmd_render,
    63	                produces=[file_output("video", "iteration.mp4")],
    64	                cost=local_zero,
    65	            ),
    66	        ],
    67	    )
    68

    72	    run_root: Path,
    73	    target_run_id: str,

# Render callsite inventory — `astrid.packs.rendering.executors.render.run`

**Grep sweep** (`executors.render`, `render_executor|render\.run|render\.py`, `rendering.render`): 26 + 29 + 60 hits. All runtime call sites are below; the rest are tests or string/id references (`rendering.render` executor id, `pipeline_step: render`).

## Verified facts
- `cut/run.py:368` & `resume.py:165` are **real bugs**: `astrid/packs/video_editing/executors/` contains only `cut/`; `from ..render.run import render` raises `ModuleNotFoundError` whenever `--render` is passed.
- `--renderer` accepts only `remotion`; declared in argparse, **not** in `executor.yaml`, and never reaches `render()` (which has `engine=`, not `renderer=`). Metadata-only.
- Provenance sidecar (`{out}.provenance.json`, payload `"output": out_path`) is written by render; `iteration_video` moves `hype.mp4` but leaves `hype.mp4.provenance.json` — **stale `output` field, missing `iteration.mp4.provenance.json`**; not in `OUTPUT_FILES`.
- `executor_argv` resolves `.py` stems by `metadata.pipeline_step`, qualified ids by registry; result cached process-wide, keyed only by name — `load_default_registry()` is *not* cached, so a mid-process fork/override yields a **stale module** from `lru_cache`.

## Unknowns
- Whether `cut --render` is exercised anywhere in prod (if not, the bug is latent); whether `iteration.mp4.provenance.json` is consumed downstream.

## Risks
- Four live bypasses escape the registry/CLI abstraction: iteration_video in-process import, iteration plan module spawn, cut/human_notes `executor_argv` module spawns, tests' in-process imports.
- Stale provenance after `hype.mp4→iteration.mp4` rename silently breaks provenance chaining.

## Suggested approach
1. Fix cut/resume to call `rendering.executors.render.run.render` (correct dotted import) or drop `--render`.
2. Route iteration_video through `astrid executors run rendering.render` (or `executor_argv("rendering.render", …)`), and rename/rewrite the provenance sidecar alongside the mp4.
3. Make `resolve_executor_runtime_module` cache-aware of registry changes (bust on override/fork) or key by registry generation.     1	# Explore: runtime callsites — every direct render import

# Render backend protocol v1

Status: **frozen M1 interoperability contract**. This document and the JSON
Schemas under `astrid/core/rendering/schemas/v1/` are the boundary that M2 SDKs,
scaffolds, and non-Python implementations must use. The schemas are normative
for wire shape; this document is normative for lifecycle and semantic rules
that JSON Schema cannot express, such as `end_frame > start_frame` and
workspace containment after symlink resolution.

This contract defines data and ownership only. Discovery, transport, the render
service, built-in backends, and installation tooling are implemented in later
batches.

## Identity, discovery, and trust

A renderer, planner, or finalizer has a qualified ID with at least one dot,
such as `rendering.remotion`, `rendering.legacy_hybrid`, or
`rendering.ffmpeg_finalizer`. IDs contain lowercase ASCII letters, digits, and
underscores. Bare `remotion` and `ffmpeg` are legacy selectors translated by
the host; `hybrid` names a planning policy and is never a renderer ID.

Packs advertise static manifests through the strict pack extension:

```yaml
extensions:
  rendering:
    renderers:
      - backends/example/renderer.yaml
    planners:
      - planners/example/planner.yaml
    finalizers:
      - finalizers/example/finalizer.yaml
```

Paths are pack-relative, must stay within the pack root after resolution, and
are parsed without importing or executing backend code. Normal pack
precedence, conflicts, aliases, overrides, and permissions apply. Only an
execution-eligible discovered candidate may run:

- source and local packs are eligible;
- an extra pack root is eligible only when explicitly supplied;
- environment-discovered packs remain inspectable but are not executable;
- an installed pack is eligible only when its active revision and installation
  trust audit are valid and its required permissions have been accepted;
- corrupt, missing, mismatched, inactive, or insufficient-permission records
  fail closed.

Trust and permission declarations do not create an operating-system sandbox.
An eligible command retains the invoking user's OS authority, subject to the
host's sanitized environment and invocation staging.

## Manifest format

The three manifest schemas are `renderer-manifest.json`,
`planner-manifest.json`, and `finalizer-manifest.json`. Their shared fields are:

| Field | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | Integer `1`; version of this manifest shape. |
| `id` | Qualified implementation ID. |
| `name` | Non-empty display name. |
| `version` | Non-empty implementation version. |
| `protocol_version` | Integer `1`; command/wire protocol implemented. |
| `command` | Non-empty argv prefix. The host appends the operation and flags. It is never evaluated by a shell. |
| `operations` | Unique supported operations. A renderer must contain `render`, a planner `plan`, and a finalizer `finalize`; `support` is optional. |
| `description` | Optional human-readable description. |
| `capabilities` | Coarse static discovery hints. Missing hints mean unknown/unsupported; a support probe is authoritative. |
| `required_permissions` | Unique subset of `project_files`, `network`, `subprocess`, `environment`, `accelerator`, and `external_services`. |
| `required_binaries` | Unique binary names checked before invocation. |
| `timeout_seconds` | Optional positive default timeout. Host policy may impose a stricter limit. |
| `metadata` | String-to-string descriptive metadata. |

Renderer capability hints cover clip and track types, boolean/string features,
whole-timeline and window support, output-profile labels, and possible audio
ownership modes. Planner hints cover named policies and fallback support.
Finalizer hints cover containers, attachment preservation, audio modes, and
features. Hints are intentionally coarse; they cannot override a request-
sensitive `SupportReport`.

Example renderer manifest:

```yaml
schema_version: 1
id: acme.example
name: Acme Example Renderer
version: 1.0.0
protocol_version: 1
command: [python3, render.py]
operations: [render, support]
description: Deterministic example renderer
data belongs in fragments, not new core fields. A new required core field,
operation, asynchronous lifecycle, different path semantics, or incompatible
media meaning requires a new protocol/schema version and parallel schemas.

M2 may wrap these types, provide helpers, scaffold code, and improve error
presentation. It must emit the same JSON. If tooling finds a kernel defect,
M1 is amended and re-reviewed rather than creating an SDK-only dialect.

## Locked epic decisions (verbatim)

1. **Backend, planner, and finalizer are distinct concepts.** `hybrid` is a
   planning policy, not a renderer backend.
2. **The timeline remains backend-neutral.** Renderer selection is invocation
   or plan configuration, never an arbitrary module path stored in timeline
   data.
3. **Backends have qualified IDs.** Built-ins should resolve canonically as
   names such as `rendering.remotion` and `rendering.ffmpeg`; short legacy names
   remain compatibility aliases.
4. **Only trusted discovered packs contribute implementations.** Reuse existing
   pack permission, precedence, conflict, alias, and override semantics. Do not
   accept arbitrary CLI import strings.
5. **`rendering.render` remains the stable facade.** Existing pipelines should
   not need to know how a backend is loaded or invoked.
6. **Selection is deterministic and inspectable.** A render plan records the
   selected backend for every segment plus the capability evidence and reason.
7. **Unsupported requests fail closed by default.** Fallback occurs only when
   an explicit planner policy or ordered fallback list permits it.
8. **Every backend returns a validated artifact.** Finalizers consume declared
   media metadata rather than assuming that arbitrary MP4 files are compatible.
9. **Final assembly is explicit.** Ship an FFmpeg finalizer first, but keep
   finalization behind a contract so arbitrary backends do not become secretly
   coupled to inlined FFmpeg logic.
10. **Compatibility precedes semantic cleanup.** Preserve current
    `engine=remotion`, `engine=ffmpeg`, and `engine=hybrid` behavior during the
    initial rollout. A later deprecation may make explicit Remotion strict and
    move opportunistic selection to `planner=auto`.
11. **Provenance has core-owned keys and backend-owned fragments.** Backend
    fragments cannot overwrite core identity, routing, input, segment, or
    finalizer fields.
12. **No concrete backend imports outside the rendering implementation.**
    External callers use the capability runner or one public render service.
13. **The canonical interoperability boundary is language-neutral.** A
    versioned command/JSON request-result protocol is the source of truth;
    Python SDK types and helpers wrap it rather than replacing it.
14. **Developer complexity is progressive.** The minimum local synchronous
    renderer implements one render operation. Request-sensitive support and
    custom finalizers are optional layers exposed only when needed.
    Asynchronous remote jobs are explicitly deferred beyond V1.
15. **Astrid owns plumbing.** Core services own asset resolution, temporary
    workspace allocation, output probing and normalization, audio
    passthrough/muxing, hashes, core provenance, cleanup, and replay metadata.
    Backend authors return media plus a namespaced provenance fragment.
16. **Static capabilities are coarse discovery hints, not the final verdict.**
    A request-sensitive support probe returns structured supported/unsupported
    features, reasons, and alternatives.
17. **Failures are replayable.** Every failed backend invocation can retain or
    emit a self-contained request bundle and exact replay command without
    rerunning the editorial pipeline.
18. **Primary video is required; attachments are extensible.** V1 planners and
    finalizers operate on a validated primary video. Optional named attachments
    are preserved in results and provenance but need not be interpreted by the
    default finalizer.
    - non-positive clip intervals or source bounds outside probed duration;
    - visual gaps and overlaps;
    - speed changes;
    - unsupported positioning, crop, effect, transition, or non-default opacity semantics;
    - requested visual audio that would be discarded;
    - overlapping audio;
    - `params.fadeIn`/`fadeOut`;
    - missing sources or required audio/video streams.
  - Implement the documented audio controls that are cheap and exact:
    - effective gain is track volume × clip volume;
    - `track.muted` forces zero gain;
    - clip mute remains `volume: 0`; do not invent a clip-level `muted` field;
    - validate gains rather than silently clamping malformed values.
  - Let an explicit planner route unsupported windows elsewhere; strict `rendering.ffmpeg` must not silently alter them.
  - Express media optimization and audio-reactive specialization as request-sensitive support evidence, not facade branches.
  - Preserve compatible stream-copy behavior and supported sequential audio mixing.
  - Return explicit audio ownership; host compatibility policy, not third-party renderers, owns synthesized silence.
  - Use manifest-required binaries and shared subprocess/output validation.
  - Gate: support diagnostics, command graphs, stream-copy, gaps/overlaps, track mute/volume, clip volume zero, fades, source bounds, missing streams/binaries, audio-reactive marker frames/hashes, cleanup, output validation, and provenance pass with a real FFmpeg render.

## Batch 3 — Built-in renderer and finalizer extraction

**Checkpoint:** The oracle reviews the Remotion, FFmpeg, and FFmpeg-finalizer implementations behind the shared manifests and wire protocol, including concurrency, strict support diagnostics, audio semantics, real FFmpeg output, and facade compatibility. Batch 4 cannot begin until the oracle returns `PASS`.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- `rendering.remotion`, `rendering.ffmpeg`, and `rendering.ffmpeg-finalizer` are statically registered through `astrid/packs/rendering/pack.yaml` and their manifests.
- Remotion preserves `TimelineComposition`, merged themes, props, registry state/hashes, source-pack and effect lineage, effect staging, sanitized environment, cleanup, and output validation.
- One non-recursive cross-process lock spans registry-state reads, all registry/shim/theme-pointer writes, active-theme selection, the complete Remotion render, and the `gen-types` writer path.
- Strict FFmpeg support fails closed for unknown kinds, invalid bounds, visual gaps/overlaps, speed, transforms, crop, effects, transitions, opacity, discarded visual audio, overlapping audio, fades, missing streams, and missing binaries.
- FFmpeg implements exact track-volume × clip-volume gain, track mute, clip `volume: 0`, supported sequential audio mixing, stream-copy behavior, and explicit audio ownership without renderer-synthesized silence.
- The finalizer probes every segment, stream-copies only complete profile matches, otherwise normalizes dimensions, rational FPS/time base, codecs, pixel format, audio rate/layout/presence, and records each normalization.
- Existing compatibility tests, Remotion typecheck, an available Remotion fixture render, and a real FFmpeg render pass.

    62	| `tools/render_and_check.py` | 40 | canonical CLI spawn | `[py, "-m", "astrid", "executors", "run", "rendering.render", "--out", ..., "--input", "timeline=...", "--input", "assets_registry=..."]` run via `subprocess.run(render_cmd, cwd=REPO)` (line 46) — the canonical `astrid executors run rendering.render` form |
    63	
    64	Summary: no production caller today uses anything but the monolith module —
    65	either in-process (`render()` function), `python -m ...render.run` subprocess,
    66	or the canonical `astrid executors run rendering.render` CLI (which itself
    67	forks the same runtime module).
    68	
    69	## 4. Empty Sprint 08 fixture state
    70	
    71	`tests/fixtures/sprint08/` contains exactly **one file**:
    72	
    73	- `README.md` — documents that the directory is meant to hold
    74	  `createAgentWorkflowTimelineFixture` / `createEmbedDemoTimelineFixture` JSON
    75	  snapshots plus `golden/<name>.sha256` digests, and that
    76	  `tests/test_renderer_parity.py` skips itself when no fixtures/goldens are
    77	  committed.
    78	
    79	No `.json` fixtures and no `golden/` directory are present.
    80	
    81	## 5. Legacy engine dispatch in run.py
    82	
    83	Three engines, dispatched inside `render()` (lines 1400–1553):
    84	
    85	| Engine | Implementation | Defined | Dispatched |
    86	|---|---|---|---|
    87	| `remotion` | npx Remotion render (subprocess `npx remotion render <composition> --props ... --output ...` lines 1493–1510); asset HTTP server lines 1450–1457; element registry regen lines 1443, 967–994 | — | default; `engine != "remotion"` → `ValueError(f"Unsupported render engine: {engine}")` (lines 1437–1438); auto-FFmpeg check line 1439; Remotion path lines 1441–1528. Also used per-segment by hybrid at lines 856–862. |
    88	| `ffmpeg` | `_render_ffmpeg_media` (builds ffmpeg `-filter_complex` concat, lines 518–673) | line 518 | explicit `engine == "ffmpeg"` → lines 1435–1436; auto-route from nominal `remotion` → lines 1439–1440; hybrid all-ffmpeg shortcut → lines 834–835; hybrid ffmpeg segments → lines 853–854. |
    89	| `hybrid` | `_render_hybrid` (window complex regions → Remotion segments, concat via `_concat_segments`, lines 827–902) | line 827 | `engine == "hybrid"` → lines 1425–1434. |
    90	
    91	Dispatch order in `render()`: (1) audio-reactive specialization early check
    92	(lines 1415–1424), (2) `hybrid`, (3) `ffmpeg`, (4) unknown-engine ValueError,
    93	(5) nominal `remotion` with auto-FFmpeg eligibility (lines 1437–1440).
    94	
    95	CLI `--engine` choices: `("remotion", "ffmpeg", "hybrid")`, default `remotion`
    96	(line 1561).
    97	
    98	## 6. Nominal-Remotion auto-FFmpeg routing
    99	
   100	- Eligibility helper: **`_can_render_with_ffmpeg_media(timeline_path, assets_path)`**,
   101	  defined at lines 676–689: loads timeline JSON + asset registry, runs
   102	  `_validate_ffmpeg_media_timeline` (lines 491–515: exactly one visual track,
   103	  media clips only, speed == 1.0, visual clips muted (`volume == 0`),
   104	  non-overlapping audio clips), then requires ≥ 1 media clip on a visual track.
   105	  Any exception → `False`.
   106	- Used at line 1439 inside `render()` when `engine == "remotion"`: if True →
   107	  `_render_ffmpeg_media` (line 1440); else → the full Remotion path.
   108	- Net effect: a media-only timeline nominally requested with the default
   109	  `remotion` engine never launches Node; it renders via ffmpeg.
   110	
   111	## 7. Audio-reactive early selection
   112	
   113	- Module import: line 36 `from astrid.packs.rendering.executors.render import audio_reactive_colour`.
   114	  `EFFECT_ID = "audio-reactive-colour"`, `ADAPTER_ID = "audio-reactive-colour/v1"`
   115	  (audio_reactive_colour.py:14–15).
   116	- Entry predicate: `audio_reactive_colour.match_and_validate(timeline_data, registry, assets_path)`
   117	  (audio_reactive_colour.py:106–274) returns `AudioReactiveColourSpec | None`
   118	  — the strict whole-timeline contract check (exactly 2 clips = one
   119	  `audio-reactive-colour` effect clip on a single visual track + one audio
   120	  media clip, both at zero; params `schemaVersion == 1`, `initialColor`
   121	  `#RRGGBB`, strictly increasing `events` frames; audio asset must be local).
   122	- Dispatch: `_render_audio_reactive_colour_if_supported` (lines 1283–1397)
   123	  gates on: exactly 2 clips with exactly 1 effect clip (lines 1294–1304),
   124	  `_audio_reactive_ffmpeg_element(theme_path)` adapter match (lines 1269–1280,
   125	  1305–1307), then `match_and_validate` (line 1309). On success it calls
   126	  `audio_reactive_colour.render(spec, out_path)` (line 1315) and writes a
   127	  provenance sidecar with `ffmpeg_specialization` + `audio_reactive_colour`
   128	  keys (lines 1335–1358).
   129	- `render()` calls it **first**, before any engine dispatch (lines 1415–1424);
   130	  a non-None result short-circuits `engine=remotion|ffmpeg|hybrid` alike.
   131	
   132	## 8. v1 provenance keys — `_write_render_provenance`
   133	
   134	Function at lines 1173–1233. The dict construction (lines 1189–1226):
   135	
   136	```python
   137	payload: dict[str, Any] = {
   138	    "schema_version": 1,                       # line 1190
   139	    "engine": engine,                          # line 1191
   140	    "output": str(out_path.resolve()),         # line 1192
   141	    "timeline": str(timeline_path.resolve()),  # line 1193
   142	    "assets_registry": str(assets_path.resolve()),  # line 1194
   143	    "project_dir": str(project_dir.resolve()), # line 1195
   144	    "composition_id": composition_id,          # line 1196
   145	    "active_pack_order": _active_pack_order_for_provenance(),  # line 1197
   146	    "active_theme": _active_theme_for_provenance(theme_path, active_theme),  # line 1198
   147	    "registry_hash": registry_state.get("hash"),  # line 1199
   148	    "registry_state": registry_state,          # line 1200
   149	    "resolved_effect_ids": [str(effect["effect_id"]) for effect in effects if "effect_id" in effect],  # line 1201
   150	    "resolved_effects": effects,               # line 1202
   151	    "source_pack_ids": sorted({str(effect["source_pack_id"]) for effect in effects if isinstance(effect, dict) and effect.get("source_pack_id")}),  # lines 1203-1209
   152	    "element_roots": sorted({str(effect["element_root"]) for effect in effects if isinstance(effect, dict) and effect.get("element_root")}),  # lines 1210-1216
   153	    "staged_asset_ids": sorted({str(asset_id) for effect in effects if isinstance(effect, dict) for asset_id in effect.get("staged_asset_ids", ())}),  # lines 1217-1224
   154	    "staged_asset_root": stage_summary.get("root"),  # line 1225
   155	}
   156	```
   157	
   158	Conditional keys: `segments` added when `segments is not None` (lines
   159	1227–1228); `segment_provenance` added when `segment_provenance is not None`
   160	(lines 1229–1230). Written as `{out_path}.provenance.json` (sidecar path
   161	helper `_render_provenance_sidecar_path`, lines 1123–1124), `sort_keys=True`,
   162	`indent=2` (line 1232).
   163	
   164	Audio-reactive runs additionally mutate the sidecar post-write with
   165	`ffmpeg_specialization` and `audio_reactive_colour` (lines 1347–1358).
   166	
   167	## 9. Transition units
   168	
   169	- `_clip_duration_seconds(clip)` (lines 399–405): `max(0, (to - from)) / speed`;
   170	  `speed <= 0` raises `ValueError`.
   171	- `_clip_timeline_end_seconds(clip)` (lines 408–417): media clip →
   172	  `at + _clip_duration_seconds`; `hold` numeric → `at + max(0, hold)`;
   173	  numeric `to` → `to`; else `at`.
   174	- `_timeline_duration_seconds(timeline_data)` (lines 420–427): explicit
   175	  `metadata.duration_seconds` (numeric) wins; else
   176	  `metadata.expected_duration_seconds`; else `max(_clip_timeline_end_seconds
   177	  over clips, default 0.0)`.
   178	- `_round_frame_time(seconds, fps, *, mode)` (lines 430–438):
   179	  `frames = seconds * fps`; `floor` → `int(frames // 1)`, `ceil` →
   180	  `int(-(-frames // 1))`, else Python `round(frames)`; result `frame / fps`.
   181	- `_complex_clip_windows` (lines 692–763): default transition duration is
   182	  **8 frames / fps** (line 726), overridable by `transition.duration`
   183	  (seconds) or `transition.durationFrames / fps` (lines 727–731); windows are
   184	  padded by `handle_seconds=0.25` and frame-rounded (floor/ceil) (lines
   185	  734–753), then sorted + merged (lines 756–763).
   186	- `_hybrid_segments(timeline_data)` (lines 766–784): total duration =
   187	  `_round_frame_time(_timeline_duration_seconds, fps, mode="ceil")` (line
   188	  768); no complex windows → single `{"engine": "ffmpeg", "from": 0.0, "to":
   189	  duration}` (lines 770–771); otherwise alternating `ffmpeg`/`remotion`
   190	  segments clipped to `[0, duration]` (lines 772–784).
   191	
   192	## 10. Standalone vs attached run ownership
   193	
   194	- `run.py` `main()` (lines 1556–1611) **never calls
   195	  `prepare_project_run`** (from `astrid/core/project/run.py:145`) and **never
   196	  creates a `run.json`**. Verified by grep: `prepare_project_run` and
   197	  `run.json` appear nowhere in `astrid/packs/rendering/executors/render/run.py`.
   198	- Render is a **standalone, unattached** executor: it writes only the output
   199	  video (`--out`, default name `hype.mp4`), a temporary `.remotion-props.json`
   200	  (unlinked in `finally`, lines 1446/1530), staged effect assets under
   201	  `project_dir/public/astrid-effects/<render_hash>/` (removed in `finally`,
   202	  line 1531), and the provenance sidecar `{out}.provenance.json` (line 1232).
   203	- Consistent with `executor.yaml` `metadata.requires_timeline: false` (line
   204	  128) — the executor opts out of project-run attachment.
   205	- `_delete_previous_render_outputs_for_timeline` (lines 1127–1150) is the only
   206	  cross-run bookkeeping: it removes prior sibling `hype.mp4` + sidecar in
   207	  `runs/` for the same timeline, unless `--keep-previous-renders` (lines
   208	  1413–1414).
   130	
   131	def _write_timeline(tmp_path: Path, data: dict, name: str = "hype.timeline.json") -> Path:
   132	    path = tmp_path / name
   133	    path.write_text(json.dumps(data), encoding="utf-8")
   134	    return path
   135	
   136	
   137	def _write_assets(tmp_path: Path, name: str = "hype.assets.json") -> Path:
   138	    path = tmp_path / name
   139	    path.write_text(json.dumps({"assets": {}}), encoding="utf-8")
   140	    return path
